cards.name: RedotPay Card
cards.issuer: RedotPay group. Visa. Programme is assigned by country of ordinary residence: Hong Kong Programme (Visa) issued by Red F. Technology Limited (RFTL), Hong Kong, business registration 75073741, card 'categorised as a credit card under Hong Kong laws'; Singapore Programme (Visa debit) with Redotpay Technology Pte. Ltd. (RTPL), Singapore company 202346379C, acting as programme manager under card issuance services from an unnamed BIN Sponsor, for persons 'ordinarily resident outside of Singapore'. The terms pages read do not name a bank.
cards.thailand_evidence: Thailand is absent from all four RedotPay exclusion lists read on 2026-09-23: 'Unsupported Countries/Regions' (by citizenship; updated over 3 weeks before 2026-09-23), 'Card Issuance Restrictions' (by residence: 'Residents of these areas are ineligible for both virtual and physical cards'; updated over 3 weeks before 2026-09-23), 'Card Delivery Restrictions' (physical card shipping; dated July 21, 2026) and 'Location-Based Access Restrictions'. RedotPay publishes exclusion lists, not an allow-list, so this status rests on Thailand's absence from those lists.
cards.nationality_note: Two separate tests. KYC is refused to citizens of listed countries, including United States, Mainland China, Myanmar, Russia, Ukraine, Iran, North Korea, Venezuela and others (citizenship list). Card issuance is refused to residents of listed places, which add India, Indonesia, Morocco, Nepal, Singapore and Turkey. Thai nationals do not appear on either list. A foreign resident of Thailand holding a passport from a listed country (for example a US citizen) fails the citizenship test. KYC: original physical ID (search-result snippets from the help centre name passport, identity card or driver's licence, and say residence permits are generally not supported), valid at least 3 months, residential address required, age 18+.

fees.issue: Virtual card 10 USD; physical card 100 USD (help centre, July 27, 2026). Deducted from account balance.
fees.annual: None stated on the help-centre fee articles read. HK and SG terms say a renewal fee may be charged 'as indicated on the App'.
fees.fx: 1.2% for transactions in a different currency; 1% crypto conversion fee (help centre ATM/fees article, July 27, 2026). Separate 1.5% transaction fee (minimum 0.50 USD) at listed merchants such as Facebook Ads, Discord, PUBG Mobile, first 3 eligible transactions per card per month waived.
fees.atm: HKD card: 2%. USD card: 2% up to 10,000 USD per month, 3% above that (help centre, July 27, 2026). ATM operator fees not addressed.
fees.topup: Crypto deposit fee not stated on pages read; minimum deposits and networks shown only in the app. Card-funding fee article could not be fetched (redirect loop).

cards.atm_limit: Not readable on the provider's fee page (the table is an image). Third-party search snippets conflict: 100,000 USD per transaction and 1,000,000 USD per day (transferfees.io / cryptocardhub) versus 50,000 USD per month and 3,750 USD per day (spendnode.io). Physical card only for ATM use per the same snippets.
cards.spend_limit: Not readable on the provider's fee page. Third-party search snippets report 100,000 USD per transaction and 1,000,000 USD per day. Terms say limits are set by RTPL/RFTL and shown in the app.
cards.assets: USDT, USDC, BTC, ETH 'and more' (help centre, July 21, 2026); networks shown only on the in-app deposit page. RedotPay news pages state USDT on TRON and USDC/USDT withdrawals to Solana.
cards.apple_google_pay: Google Pay and PayPal linking supported per help centre. Apple Pay: from August 22, 2025, new Apple Pay enablement for Hong Kong 'Cards-as-a-Service' programmes was suspended; cards already added keep working (help centre, July 21, 2026). A July 22, 2026 help article describes adding a card to Apple Pay after a free card 'upgrade' but does not say which cards or regions qualify.

affiliate.terms: User referral (in-app 'Invite Friends', help centre July 26, 2026): rewards in USDT; card-order commission as a percentage of the friend's card fee, payment commission as a percentage of the friend's card spend (settled after 30 days), secondary commission of 10% of a referred user's commission; levels raise the rates; exact percentages not stated in text. Affiliate programme (redotpay.com/affiliates, undated): 'up to 40% commission', four levels, instant commission on card applications, apply in app/website with identity verification. Level-by-level rates appear only as an image in the December 23, 2024 news post.

Custody partners named in platform terms (effective Jul 7, 2026): Tazapay, BitGo 'or others'.
cards.thailand_evidence: KAST publishes no country list; its help centre (updated 2026-08-09) says supported countries are those in the sign-up dropdown: 'If you don't see your country in the dropdown menu, we haven't launched there yet.' The in-app list was not viewed (no sign-up). The help centre supports THB payouts to Thai bank accounts (1% FX, 2 USD fixed fee, minimum 50 THB) 'from any country supported by KAST', which concerns payouts, not residency. Thailand is absent from KAST's Apple Pay availability list (2026-09-10).
cards.nationality_note: Platform terms bar anyone 'located in, or a national or resident of any Restricted Locations'; the help centre says a person living in a supported country but holding only an ID from a restricted region may fail KYC, and dual citizens may use an ID from a supported country. Residency means where you legally live and hold proof of address dated within 3 months. KYC: passport, national ID or driver's licence; live selfie; proof of address (utility bill, bank statement, government letter or lease).

fees.issue: Standard: 2 virtual cards included (a $2 issuance fee applies in some regions, including for included cards); additional virtual card $2; physical card $0 card fee + $40 delivery fee. Premium/Private cards included with membership (help centre, 2026-09-01).
fees.annual: Membership: Standard $0; Premium $1,000 per year; Private $10,000 per year (help centre, 2026-09-10). Conflict: the non-US cardholder agreement (effective Mar 20, 2025) lists 'Annual Fees: up to USD 20'.
fees.fx: 0.5%–1.75% on non-USD transactions, varying by residence country, transaction country and card programme; $0.10 on non-USD transactions under $25; $0.50 on declines for insufficient balance (help centre, 2026-09-01). Conflict: cardholder agreement (Mar 20, 2025) says FX 'up to 2%' and low-transaction fee USD 0.2.
fees.atm: $3 flat + 2% of amount; non-USD also pays the FX fee.
fees.topup: Top-up fee 0%; stablecoin deposit fee 0% excluding blockchain network fees; stablecoins credited 1:1 to USD with 0% spread.

cards.atm_limit: Up to $250 per withdrawal including fees; up to 3 withdrawals or $750 per rolling 24 hours.
cards.spend_limit: No fixed card transaction, deposit or balance limit ('Unlimited'); spending capped by balance; large transactions may face compliance review; user-set limits available in app.
cards.assets: Receive USDT on Solana, Ethereum, Tron, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain, Arbitrum, Avalanche C-Chain, TON; USDC on Solana, Ethereum, Polygon, Base, Stellar, Arbitrum, Avalanche C-Chain, Optimism, Sonic; PYUSD (Ethereum, Solana); RLUSD (Ethereum, XRPL); plus BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB and other tokens (help centre, 2026-09-10). Balance held in USD.
cards.apple_google_pay: Apple Pay depends on registered country of residence; the published list (2026-09-10) includes Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Vietnam and others but not Thailand. Google Pay setup article exists (2026-08-09); no country list for Google Pay seen.

affiliate.pays_in: USD (credited to the in-app Rewards balance)
affiliate.terms: User referral (2026-09-10): referrer earns up to $20 / $30 / $50 / $150 as the referee's cumulative card spend reaches $100 / $600 / $1,600 / $6,600 (total up to $250), plus $100 or $1,000 when the referee buys Premium or Private; 14-day lock; amounts vary by referee country. Affiliate programme (application + approval): tiers by active referrals (5 / 50 / 100 / 500 users); spend-milestone rewards up to $20–$40 at $100 spend rising to $250–$500 at $6,600 spend; subscription commission $100–$200 (Premium) and $1,000–$2,000 (Private); ongoing cashback on referrals' card transactions; rewards depend on referral's country.

other_rails.name: TouristDigiPay (Thai SEC regulatory sandbox)
other_rails.what: A sandbox run under the Thai SEC with the Ministry of Finance, the Anti-Money Laundering Office and the Ministry of Tourism and Sports, announced 18 August 2025. A foreign visitor opens two accounts once in Thailand: one with an SEC-licensed digital asset exchange, broker or dealer, and one e-money wallet with a Bank of Thailand-licensed e-money operator. Crypto is converted to THB in the wallet and spent at merchants by QR; crypto is not paid to merchants and cash withdrawal is not permitted. Reported timeline: rules effective 24 September 2025; operator applications 25 September to 26 December 2025; go-live expected Q4 2025; sandbox period up to 18 months. Unused THB can be converted back to digital assets through the same operator and sent to the original wallet (Thairath, 18 August 2025). The scheme extends the earlier Phuket Sandbox (Thairath). Participants: Bitkub Exchange announced it joined, planning account opening for foreign visitors and e-money partners at airports (Bangkok Biz News press release, 20 August 2025); a January 2026 guide names SCBX's Rubie Wallet; no official participant list was read. Status as of September 2026: reported as a live pilot running into early 2027; the SEC's site returned HTTP 403 to the fetch, so current status and participant list are not confirmed.
other_rails.cost: Limits reported: 50,000 THB per person per month for payments to small vendors (no know-your-merchant check); up to 500,000 THB per person per month at merchants that completed know-your-merchant. Operators must notify the SEC if a single conversion exceeds 450,000 THB (AIM Bangkok). One guide (Sabaifly) also states 100,000 THB per transaction; single source. Conversion fees not found.
other_rails.for_foreigners: For foreign visitors staying in Thailand temporarily (AIM Bangkok's wording, paraphrased). No source read names visa types or states how long-stay foreign residents are treated; unclear whether DTV, retirement or work-visa holders qualify. KYC and customer due diligence required; for monthly amounts above 50,000 THB per person, operators check the source of the digital assets with blockchain forensic tools.
